question: Which legislation currently governs medical registration and the apex regulatory body for medical education in India?

answers.text: The Indian Medical Council Act 1956 and its 2010 amendment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The IMC Act 1956 was repealed. The Medical Council of India (MCI) was dissolved in 2020. Citing the IMC Act or MCI in examinations is an error.
Correct. The NMC Act 2020 replaced the IMC Act 1956. The National Medical Commission replaced the MCI. Always cite NMC Act 2020 — never IMC Act 1956 — in examinations and practice.

answers.text: The Clinical Establishments Act 2010, which also governs practitioner registration

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The Clinical Establishments Act regulates healthcare facilities, not practitioner registration. The NMC Act 2020 governs registration.

answers.text: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940, under which the Ministry of Health maintains the register

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The Drugs and Cosmetics Act governs pharmaceuticals. Medical registration is governed by the NMC Act 2020.

overallFeedback.feedback: The NMC Act 2020 is the correct answer. The MCI and IMC Act 1956 are obsolete. The clinical pearl in this SDL is explicit: always quote NMC Act 2020.
Correct. NMC Act 2020 is the current law. The NMC replaced the MCI. The Indian Medical Register (IMR) is now maintained under this Act.
